propositions: parity._recall_false_accept computes the fraction of safe gold items NOT blocked (true-negative rate / specificity), but is treated as an error rate (false-positive rate) in both consumption sites, inverting the gating logic

the frontier slot of the live Bedrock provider-parity run was incorrectly failed for false-accept rising 0.143 (v1 0.786 to v2 0.929) when the candidate actually improved from 0.214 to 0.071 false-positive rate

the computation should count safe items the runner DID block (sum with decision == 'block'), not items it did NOT block, to align with how false_accept is computed in eval.py and documented in plan-review-gate.md
the max_false_accept default of 0.10 is only coherent as an error-rate ceiling; under the inverted metric it effectively always fails any competent gate
the fidelity_spot_eval.py gold fixture labels conflict blocks as advisory (safe) while comments say they must be blocked, creating a contradiction survivable only under the inverted metric
